abstract: Language models are sequential processors, but long-horizon agency requires external information and computation beyond model weights and active context. Prime Agent is an open-source harness for long-horizon evaluation and coding-agent workflows. A persistent IPython REPL follows the Recursive Language Model abstraction for programmatic context processing and test-time compute, while Continual Harness preserves histories, memories, skills, prompts, and subagent specifications across trajectories. Recursive subagents coordinate through direct agent-to-agent communication, and the Agents View lets humans inspect and manage daemon-backed sessions. Prime Agent standardizes execution, recovery, verification, and resource accounting while leaving strategy construction to the model. This low-friction, expressive membrane prevents harness failures from becoming model failures and pushes measurement toward the model’s true maximal underlying capability. Prime Agent raises ARC-AGI-3 RHAE Best@1 from 30% to 95.5% and matches or exceeds native and popular harnesses across long-context coding, GPU-kernel generation, emulator construction, and autonomous nanoGPT speedruns. On Factorio, we find refinement allows for continuous technology progression and dedicated subagents enable parallelized work. Code is available at https://github.com/PrimeIntellect-ai/prime-agent.

sections.body: The introduction argues that a language model is a bounded sequential processor, so a harness must supply external state and computation. It describes four state levels: weights (L0), active context (L1), a persistent REPL with recursive subagents (L2), and disk-backed history, memories, and skills (L3). Prime Agent pairs standardized execution with a low-friction interface, so a model should fail an evaluation only when the task exceeds its capability. The introduction reports ARC-AGI-3 performance improving from 30% to 95%, and an 85.5-hour nanoGPT run with 19 validated records. These are summary claims; the detailed evidence appears in Section 3.
sections.heading: 1 Introduction
sections.headline: Prime Agent argues the harness should expose expressive primitives, so evaluation measures model capability rather than harness failures.

sections.body: Prime Agent separates information management, which decides what state enters a model call, from computation management, which maps model-selected actions to code, tools and subagent sessions. State sits in four levels: weights (L0), active context (L1), the persistent IPython REPL with recursive subagents (L2), and disk-backed storage (L3). The asynchronous `rlm` primitive creates a subagent and returns a handle before it completes. A daemon keeps sessions alive when clients detach, and queues carry agent-to-agent messages. Continual Harness stores prompts, memories, skills and subagent specifications, applies edits at turn boundaries, and keeps versions for rollback. This section reports no quantitative results.
sections.heading: 2 Prime Agent Architecture
sections.headline: Prime Agent splits information management from computation management across persistent sessions, a daemon and Continual Harness state.

sections.body: The evaluation asks whether test-time tokens convert into ARC-AGI-3 progress, whether persistent REPL state helps long-context work, and whether the runtime sustains multi-day runs. On ARC-AGI-3, output tokens and cost convert into progress at sharply different rates across configurations. Table 1 reports point estimates for nine long-context tasks with no uncertainty intervals. On the nanoGPT speedrun, harness choice has little effect on final records compared with experimental noise, but models run more out-of-loop experiments under Prime Agent. The authors state that their Claude Code and Codex ARC runs fell below self-reported scores, so those reference values are external.
sections.heading: 3 Evaluation
sections.headline: Prime Agent is generally competitive on long-context tasks and close to native harnesses on GPU-kernel generation.

sections.body: Related work covers four areas. Programmatic inference gives models code and recursive calls for context and compute, and memory methods retain skills and traces. Coding-agent runtimes and long-horizon benchmarks measure tasks over many steps. ARC-AGI-3 community systems build world models and preserve procedures. Multi-agent and human-agent work studies role prompts, messages and communication. The section positions Prime Agent as integrating these mechanisms, adding persistent kernels, recursive sessions, recovery, and complete trajectory capture. It reports no experimental results.
sections.heading: 4 Related Work
sections.headline: Prior work spans programmatic inference, coding-agent runtimes, ARC-AGI-3 systems and multi-agent communication, which Prime Agent combines.

sections.body: The conclusion frames Prime Agent as one substrate joining persistent execution, recursive sessions, autonomous controls, recorded history and Continual Harness. It states that the results show this substrate supports different forms of test-time computation under standardized execution and accounting. It names remaining friction: models still struggle to allocate subagents, manage retained information and refine reusable state. The authors expect model-harness co-learning to become the main route to new long-horizon capabilities. They suggest training directly with Prime Agent, and targeted training on the RLM and Continual Harness components to isolate their contributions.
sections.heading: 5 Conclusion
sections.headline: Many harness capabilities remain underused because current models were not trained to operate them.

sections.body: Appendix A reproduces one out-of-loop experiment per model from the nanoGPT runs in Section 3.3. Kimi K3 re-derives Newton–Schulz iteration coefficients with a global optimizer and checks bf16 rounding bit-exactly. DeepSeek V4 Pro builds a calibrated toy of the training problem. GLM 5.3 debugs its SOAP implementation on CPU before any GPU screen. Appendix B gives an orchestration example and states that a child is a persistent concurrent session, not a stateless completion returned by `rlm`. Appendix C discloses that language models assisted with code development, writing refinement and formatting, and that the authors hold the scientific claims.
sections.heading: Appendix
sections.headline: The appendix lists three out-of-loop nanoGPT experiments, from Kimi K3, DeepSeek V4 Pro and a third model, plus an orchestration example.
